data.title: Meduza: ‘We do whatever we want with what’s ours’: A look back at Ukraine’s attacks on the Crimean Bridge
data.summary: Since the start of the full-scale war, the Crimean Bridge, which links the Russian-annexed peninsula to Russia’s Krasnodar region, has repeatedly been a target of Ukrainian strikes. Ukrainian officials have stressed that they target the bridge because it is used for military purposes. In November, new Ukrainian strikes destroyed an arch on the bridge’s road section, and the debris blocked the shipping channel. It was the most damaging strike yet, and Russian authorities have not given even a rough timeline for repairs. But Ukraine’s military had also done significant damage to the bridge in earlier years. Below are photos of the aftermath of both the earlier and latest attacks.

data.title: Meduza: ‘This was no Yalta’: How the world’s press read the Trump–Putin–Xi summit in China
data.summary: The leaders of Russia, the United States, and China met in person for the first time on November 19 in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Symbolically, the meeting was unprecedented, but in substance it produced modest results: Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, and Donald Trump talked for an hour and a half and adopted a declaration that touches on several important issues but sticks to general language. Commentators concluded that the summit was no repeat of the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain, and the United States divided postwar Europe into spheres of influence. Meduza has gathered what outlets in the United States, Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and China are saying about the summit.
